bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Marion R.(Ritvo) (Miller) Fremont-Smith (1926-2021) was a lawyer, legal scholar, and authority on the law of foundations and nonprofit organizations. A 1948 graduate of Wellesley College, she received her JD cum laude from Boston University Law School in 1951. While raising her children in the 1950s, she taught political science at Wellesley. In 1958 she helped to establish a Division of Civil Rights and Civil Liberties in the Massachusetts Office of the Attorney General. In December 1960 she was named Massachusetts Special Assistant Attorney General, Director of the Division of Public Charities, and served as well on the Attorney General's Advisory Committee on Public Charities.

In 1963, Marion R. Fremont-Smith became a project director for the Russell Sage Foundation, undertaking a detailed study of the Public Accountability of Charitable Foundations, which resulted in her 1965 volume, "Foundations and Government: State and Federal Law and Supervision." She followed up this study with an exploration of "Philanthropy and the Business Corporation" (Russell Sage Foundation, 1972).

Ms. Fremont-Smith joined the Boston law firm of Choate, Hall and Stewart as an associate in 1964, and she was elected partner in 1971 (becoming one of the first female partners in a Boston law firm). Specializing in tax-exempt organizations, trusts, and estates, she was an active participant in professional organizations such as the American Bar Association, the Council on Foundations, and Independent Sector. Marion R. Fremont-Smith provided testimony, opinions, and legal advice to Congressional investigations, agencies, commissions, and professional panels, at a time when tax-exempt organizations were receiving scrutiny from several quarters.

In 1998, Ms. Fremont-Smith returned to academia as a senior research fellow at the Hauser Center for Nonprofit Organizations, at Harvard's Kennedy School, and as a lecturer at Harvard Law School. In 2004, she published her third book, "Governing Nonprofit Organizations." She was also Co-Reporter and Consultant on the American Law Institute's first "Restatement of the Law, Charitable Nonprofit Organizations," published in 2021.
Marion R. Fremont-Smith held several other professional or governance roles during her long career:
Chair of the American Bar Association's Section on Taxation, Committee on Exempt Organizations.
Member of the IRS Commission and Advisory Group on Exempt Organizations.
Director of the Council on Foundations.
Trustee of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace.
Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Marion R. Fremont-Smith papers document her career and significant role in advocating for and helping to shape the law of nonprofit organizations. The collection particularly documents her activities in connection with the Massachusetts Advisory Committee on Public Charities; her research for the Russell Sage Foundation on charitable trusts and foundations and the resulting publication of "Foundations and Government" in 1965; and her follow-up study on "Philanthropy and the Business Corporation," 1972. The papers also include a digital manuscript of her third book, "Governing Nonprofit Organizations," published in 2004.

The papers document Marion R. Fremont-Smith's outreach to attorneys general of other states and the professional connections she built through her research. She actively participated in professional organizations (such as the National Association of Attorneys General, the American Bar Association and its Taxation Section Committee on Exempt Organizations, and the Council on Foundations), presented at conferences and other programs, and served as a leader, expert, and mentor in nonprofit law. The collection includes her articles, opinions, testimony, and name on meeting rosters and program agendas. But her specific roles in these professional organizations are not always evident in the collection. Similarly, the collection does not include a bibliography or complete file of her writings. There is correspondence pertaining to her Russell Sage Foundation projects, but otherwise there is little concerning her later career, personal life, or her practice at Choate, Hall and Stewart.

Later materials concern Marion R. Fremont-Smith's participation in the Panel on the Nonprofit Sector's Advisory Committee on Self Regulation (for Independent Sector) and in the Emerging Issues in Philanthropy seminars at the Hauser Center for Nonprofit Organizations at Harvard's Kennedy School, where Fremont-Smith was senior research fellow.

did.unittitle: Marion R. Fremont-Smith - Personal and Professional Files and Writings

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series 1 of Marion R. Fremont-Smith's papers contains a few files of personally and professionally significant materials, such as appointment letters, correspondence (mainly concerning Russell Sage Foundation projects), book reviews, partnership congratulations, and two portrait photos. The series also includes various articles concerning the regulation of philanthropy published by Marion R. Fremont-Smith from 1983 to 2014. (This selection is not comprehensive; see Series 5 for other articles and writings.) A 1965 manuscript, entitled Foundations under Siege, lacks attribution but is presumably also by Marion R. Fremont-Smith.

In 2004, Marion R. Fremont-Smith published a third book entitled "Governing Nonprofit Organizations: Federal and State Law and Regulation" (Harvard University Press), which took a new look at her original 1965 study of "Foundations and Government." A digital copy of her submitted manuscript (and various drafts) are included in this series.
Finally, the series includes a small file of Children's Stories, also lacking attribution.

did.unittitle: Massachusetts, Office of the Attorney General, Division of Public Charities

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series 2 documents Marion R. Fremont-Smith's work with the Massachusetts attorney general's office as an assistant attorney general and Director of the Division of Public Charities, and as a member of the Advisory Committee on Public Charities, from 1960 through 1962. Records include correspondence and reports, plus a Survey of Public Charities in Massachusetts (1961). There are advisory committee records from 1961-1962, plus advisory committee correspondence and/or meeting records from 1977-1998, though it is not known to what extent Marion R. Fremont-Smith was involved with the committee in these later years. She left the attorney general's office at the end of 1962, to begin full-time work as a research director at the Russell Sage Foundation.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series 3 documents Marion R. Fremont-Smith's research and writing of "Foundations and Government: State and Federal Law and Supervision," which she undertook with the support and on behalf of the Russell Sage Foundation. Materials include her proposal and correspondence with the Russell Sage Foundation and other colleagues; correspondence and reference files relating to her survey of state regulations; and manuscript drafts, revisions, and proofs. The Russell Sage Foundation also funded a side project to gather and study data from the California Registry of Charitable Trusts.
The series also documents her outreach and presentations of her findings to professional organizations and conferences.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series 5 is a general series that reflects the range of Marion R. Fremont-Smith's professional engagements in nonprofit law. Materials include reports and investigations - and the responses of nonprofit leaders - from the Treasury Report in 1965, to the Patman investigations in the mid-1960s, the Tax Reform Act of 1969, Senate Finance Committee investigations of nonprofits in 1973-1974, and the House Ways and Means Oversight Subcommittee in the late 1980s. Organizations represented include the Council on Foundations; the Commission on Private Philanthropy and Public Needs (Filer Commission), 1974-1977; and the American Bar Association's Committees on Nonprofit Corporations and on Exempt Organizations, 1980s-1990s (Model Nonprofit Corporations; UBIT, Lobbying, Solicitation, and Nonprofit Governance).

In addition to documenting Marion R. Fremont-Smith's professional activities, Series 5 includes reference materials and background literature on foundations and nonprofits in general; corporate philanthropy (including education; social reform; and a proposed study of corporate contributions in the Boston area); taxation; trusts and estates; etc. Other materials include files relating to the Japanese Philanthropy project, 1974-1978, a symposium and exchange program in which Marion R. Fremont-Smith participated.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Independent Sector is a membership and advocacy group for charitable and nonprofit organizations. In October 2004, it convened a Panel on the Nonprofit Sector, to provide responses to the Senate Finance Committee on ways to improve oversight and governance of charitable organizations. Marion R. Fremont-Smith served on Independent Sector's Ethics and Accountability Committee in 2003-2004, and on the Panel's Advisory Committee on Self-Regulation in 2006-2007. Earlier materials include her 1988 paper on Accountability of the Independent Sector.
